rationale: Both documents treat the source (Raman et al. 2026 / 'white-bear steering', referred to as WBS in the message) as a credited basis: the write-up names it explicitly and says the stance-steering idea is 'prompted by' it, while the message refers to it only as 'WBS' and gives identical quantitative comparisons (cosine ~0.77, dose k=12 vs ~6-8, reproduction score 0.69). The main difference is that the write-up explicitly credits the source for inspiring the core idea, whereas the message, despite naming WBS and matching the numbers, never states that the underlying approach itself was prompted by or derived from the source, instead emphasizing 'a new contribution rather than a reproduction.'
